key_terms.حَمٓ: Disjointed letters Ha and Mim, appearing at the start of Surah Ash-Shura.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the disjointed letters Ha Mim in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Surah Ash-Shura, these disjointed letters (al-Huruf al-Muqatta'at) serve as an introductory marker to a chapter rich in theological and social guidance, emphasizing the Quran's divine origin amidst the Prophet's struggles with his community. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi in *Majma' al-Bayan*, often view these letters as a rhetorical device to capture attention before revealing the core principles of consultation (Shura) and divine unity. This placement underscores the miraculous nature of the text while linking the esoteric mystery of the letters to the exoteric clarity of its legal and spiritual teachings.
